errors.name: Jesse Owens
errors.reason: Owens' competitive track career was in the 1930s (peak 1935-36 Big Ten/Olympics); he was stripped of amateur status after 1936 and never competed prominently in the 1940s. Appears in TWO statements: one with Jackie Robinson/Joe DiMaggio/Ted Williams, one with Gordie Howe/Joe DiMaggio/Ted Williams.

naming_notes: Las Vegas Raiders (4 statements): Jerry Rice, Randy Moss, Charles Woodson, Marshawn Lynch played in Oakland; Ronnie Lott and Eric Dickerson in Los Angeles — same franchise, pre-Vegas eras.
Los Angeles Chargers (3 statements): Johnny Unitas (1973), Drew Brees, LaDainian Tomlinson, Junior Seau, Philip Rivers all played as San Diego Chargers — same franchise, pre-LA move.
Tennessee Titans (4 statements): Earl Campbell played only for the Houston Oilers era of the franchise.
Los Angeles Rams: Kurt Warner and Marshall Faulk played for the St. Louis-era Rams — same franchise.
Atlanta Braves (4 statements): Babe Ruth played for the 1935 Boston Braves and Cy Young for the 1911 Boston Rustlers — Braves franchise, but never in Atlanta.

Washington Nationals: Pedro Martinez, Pete Rose, and Randy Johnson played only for the Montreal Expos (the pre-2005 identity of the franchise) and never wore a Washington uniform; only Max Scherzer was an actual National. Strongest franchise-naming stretch in the set.
Arizona Cardinals: Jim Thorpe played for the 1928 Chicago Cardinals — same franchise, different city/era.
St. Louis Cardinals: Cy Young's St. Louis stint (1899-1900) began when the club was still the Perfectos; it took the Cardinals name in 1900, his final season there.

Dominican Republic Athletes: Vladimir Guerrero Jr. was born in Montreal, Canada; he is of Dominican heritage, was raised partly in the DR, and represents the DR internationally — borderline nationality claim.
WNBA Forwards: Sheryl Swoopes is commonly listed as a guard or guard-forward rather than a pure forward — borderline positional fit.
